metadata.title: Reconciling modern machine learning practice and the bias-variance trade-off

nodes.name: Empirical Risk Minimization (ERM)
nodes.statement: Given training data $(x_1,y_1),\dotsc,(x_n,y_n)$, ERM picks $h \in \cH$ minimizing the empirical risk $\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n \ell(h(x_i), y_i)$, where $\ell$ is a loss (e.g. squared loss).
nodes.statement_clean: Empirical risk minimization selects the predictor in the hypothesis class that minimizes average loss on the training set.

nodes.name: True (test) risk
nodes.statement: The true risk of $h$ is $\E_{(x,y)\sim P}[\ell(h(x),y)]$, expected loss under the data distribution $P$ over $\R^d \times \R$.
nodes.statement_clean: Expected loss of a predictor under the underlying data-generating distribution.

nodes.name: Bias-variance trade-off
nodes.statement: Conventional principle: capacity of $\cH$ must balance under-fitting (small $\cH$, large empirical risk) and over-fitting (large $\cH$, low empirical risk but large true risk).
nodes.statement_clean: Classical principle that hypothesis-class capacity should balance underfitting against overfitting.
nodes.origin_citation: Geman, Bienenstock, Doursat 1992; Hastie, Tibshirani, Friedman 2001

nodes.name: Interpolation threshold
nodes.statement: The capacity level at which a learned predictor first achieves zero training risk (perfect fit to the training data); for many parametric families this occurs near $N = n$.
nodes.statement_clean: Smallest model capacity at which the predictor exactly fits the training data.

nodes.name: Double descent risk curve
nodes.statement: Unified test-risk-vs-capacity curve: a classical U-shape below the interpolation threshold, a peak at the threshold, and a second descent in the over-parametrized regime, in which test risk decreases with capacity.
nodes.statement_clean: Risk curve combining the classical U-shape with a second decreasing branch beyond the interpolation threshold.

nodes.name: Random Fourier Features (RFF) class $\cHN$
nodes.statement: $\cHN = \{ h(x) = \sum_{k=1}^N a_k \phi(x;v_k) : a_k \in \mathbb{C} \}$ where $\phi(x;v) := e^{\sqrt{-1}\langle v,x\rangle}$ and $v_1,\dotsc,v_N$ are i.i.d. standard normal in $\R^d$.
nodes.statement_clean: Two-layer network with random fixed Fourier-basis first-layer weights and trainable output coefficients.

nodes.name: Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Space $\rkhs$ (Gaussian kernel)
nodes.statement: RKHS associated with the Gaussian kernel; $\cHN \to \rkhs$ as $N \to \infty$, and $\optninf$ denotes the minimum-norm interpolant in $\rkhs$.
nodes.statement_clean: Function space associated with the Gaussian kernel; limit of RFF classes as the number of features grows.

nodes.name: Random ReLU Features class
nodes.statement: $\cHN = \{ h(x) = \sum_{k=1}^N a_k \phi(x;v_k) \}$ where $\phi(x;v) := \max(\langle v,x\rangle, 0)$ and the $v_k$ are i.i.d. uniform on the unit sphere in $\R^d$.
nodes.statement_clean: Random-feature class using ReLU non-linearities with random sphere-sampled directions.

nodes.name: Fill distance $\kappa_n$
nodes.statement: $\kappa_n := \max_{x\in\Omega} \min_{x_j} \|x - x_j\|$, the largest distance from any point in $\Omega$ to its nearest sample.
nodes.statement_clean: Worst-case distance from a domain point to the nearest training sample.

nodes.name: Inductive bias (smallest-norm interpolant)
nodes.statement: Among all interpolating predictors, prefer the one of smallest function-space norm; an Occam's-razor-style preference for the simplest fit.
nodes.statement_clean: Preference for the smoothest/smallest-norm function that interpolates the data.

nodes.name: ERM with squared loss in $\cHN$
nodes.statement: Compute $\optnN \in \arg\min_{h \in \cHN} \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n (h(x_i) - y_i)^2$; if the minimizer is non-unique (e.g. $N>n$), pick the coefficient vector $(a_1,\dotsc,a_N)$ of minimum $\ell_2$ norm as a proxy for the RKHS norm.
nodes.statement_clean: Find the minimum-coefficient-norm empirical-squared-loss minimizer in the random-feature class.

nodes.name: RFF predictor form
nodes.statement: $h(x) = \sum_{k=1}^N a_k \phi(x;v_k)$, $\phi(x;v) = e^{\sqrt{-1}\langle v,x\rangle}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Linear combination of complex exponentials with random frequencies.

nodes.name: Wendland-type interpolation bound
nodes.statement: $\sup_{x \in \Omega} |h(x) - h^*(x)| < A e^{-B(n/\log n)^{1/d}} (\|h^*\|_\rkhs + \|h\|_\rkhs)$ for absolute constants $A,B>0$.
nodes.statement_clean: Sup-norm error of an interpolant in RKHS decays exponentially in the fill distance.

nodes.name: Approximation Theorem for RKHS interpolants (Theorem 1)
nodes.statement: Fix $h^* \in \rkhs$. With $x_i$ i.i.d. uniform on a compact cube $\Omega \subset \R^d$ and $y_i = h^*(x_i)$, there exist absolute constants $A,B>0$ such that for any interpolant $h \in \rkhs$ (i.e. $h(x_i)=y_i$), with high probability $\sup_{x\in\Omega} |h(x)-h^*(x)| < A e^{-B(n/\log n)^{1/d}}(\|h^*\|_\rkhs + \|h\|_\rkhs)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Any RKHS interpolant of a smooth target on a compact cube approximates it with sup-norm error decaying exponentially in $(n/\log n)^{1/d}$, scaled by the sum of RKHS norms.
assumptions: $x_i$ i.i.d. uniform on a compact cube $\Omega \subset \R^d$
conclusions: $\sup_{x \in \Omega} |h(x) - h^*(x)| < A e^{-B(n/\log n)^{1/d}}(\|h^*\|_\rkhs + \|h\|_\rkhs)$ with high probability

nodes.name: Proof sketch of Theorem 1
nodes.statement: Bound the fill $\kappa_n = O((n/\log n)^{-1/d})$ with high probability via grid+union bound; apply Wendland's Theorem 11.22 to $f := h - h^*$, using $f(x_i)=0$ and $\|f\|_\rkhs \le \|h^*\|_\rkhs + \|h\|_\rkhs$.
nodes.statement_clean: Combine a high-probability fill-distance bound with Wendland's RKHS interpolation theorem applied to the difference $h - h^*$.

nodes.name: Bound the fill distance
nodes.statement: Show that with high probability $\kappa_n = O((n/\log n)^{-1/d})$ by partitioning $\Omega$ into a grid and applying a union bound over the cells.

nodes.name: Introduce difference function $f := h - h^*$
nodes.statement: Define $f(x) := h(x) - h^*(x)$; observe $f(x_i)=0$ and by the triangle inequality $\|f\|_\rkhs \le \|h^*\|_\rkhs + \|h\|_\rkhs$.

nodes.name: Apply Wendland Theorem 11.22 to $f$
nodes.statement: Wendland's Theorem 11.22 bounds $\sup_x |f(x)|$ by an exponentially decaying factor in $\kappa_n$ times $\|f\|_\rkhs$; substitute the fill bound from Step 1 and the norm bound from Step 2 to conclude.

nodes.name: Wendland Theorem 11.22 (cited)
nodes.statement: For functions in the Gaussian-kernel RKHS that vanish on a sample with fill $\kappa_n$, the sup-norm is bounded by $A e^{-B/\kappa_n}$ times the RKHS norm, for absolute constants $A,B>0$.
nodes.statement_clean: Classical sup-norm interpolation-error bound for Gaussian-kernel RKHS in terms of fill distance.

nodes.name: RFF learning (minimum-coefficient-$\ell_2$-norm ERM)
nodes.statement: Compute $\optnN \in \cHN$ that minimizes the squared training loss; among minimizers (when $N>n$) pick coefficients of smallest $\ell_2$ norm as a surrogate for the RKHS norm.
output: Coefficient vector $(a_1,\dotsc,a_N) \in \mathbb{C}^N$ (or $\R^{2N}$) of minimum $\ell_2$ norm minimizing $\frac{1}{n}\sum_i (h(x_i)-y_i)^2$

nodes.name: Random ReLU Features learning
nodes.statement: Linear regression of squared loss over the Random ReLU features class; optionally with small ridge regularization $\lambda$ for numerical stability near the interpolation threshold.
input: Random directions $v_1,\dotsc,v_N$ uniform on the unit sphere in $\R^d$

nodes.name: Weight-reuse SGD for fully-connected two-layer NN
nodes.statement: Train a single-hidden-layer NN with SGD (momentum 0.95); below the interpolation threshold, initialize the first $H_1$ hidden units of a wider $H_2>H_1$-unit network from a previously trained narrower network and Gaussian-initialize the rest; above the threshold, use standard random initialization.
input: Glorot-uniform initialization for the smallest network; weights of the previously trained narrower network for $H_2 > H_1$
Step-size schedule: 10% decay every 500 epochs in the under-parametrized regime; fixed step size in the over-parametrized regime
Stopping rule: 6000 epochs, or zero classification error (under-parametrized regime)
output: Trained network with $(d+1) H + (H+1) K$ parameters realizing the predictor
Reduced training-risk variability across capacity sweeps relative to plain random initialization

nodes.name: Random Forest with capacity sweep
nodes.section: 3 Decision trees and ensemble methods; App. D
nodes.statement: Standard random forest for regression: at each split, sample $\sqrt{d}$ features; control capacity via $N_\mathsf{tree}$ and $N_\mathsf{leaf}^\mathsf{max}$; bootstrap re-sampling optionally disabled (PERT-style) to permit single-tree interpolation.
input: Number of trees $N_\mathsf{tree}$ and maximum number of leaves $N_\mathsf{leaf}^\mathsf{max}$
output: Forest predictor that averages the trees
Capacity controlled by $(N_\mathsf{tree}, N_\mathsf{leaf}^\mathsf{max})$, exhibits double-descent risk curve

nodes.name: $L_2$-boosting trees with forest averaging
nodes.statement: Gradient boosting (shrinkage 0.85) of trees with $\le 10$ leaves to interpolate the training data, then average predictions of multiple such forests trained with identical hyper-parameters; capacity is $(N_\mathsf{tree}, N_\mathsf{forest})$.
input: Number of boosting trees $N_\mathsf{tree}$ and number of forests $N_\mathsf{forest}$
output: Averaged $L_2$-boosted forest predictor exhibiting double-descent risk

nodes.name: RFF on MNIST ($n=10^4$, 10 classes)
nodes.statement: RFF predictors $\optnN$ trained on a $10^4$-point MNIST subset display the U-shape for $N<n$, a peak at $N=n=10^4$, and a second descent for $N>n$; $\optninf$ outperforms every finite-$N$ predictor.

nodes.name: RFF on CIFAR-10, 20-Newsgroups, TIMIT, SVHN
nodes.statement: RFF predictors trained on $n=10^4$ subsets of CIFAR-10, 20-Newsgroups, TIMIT, SVHN reproduce the double-descent risk curve with peak at $N=10^4$ across image, text and speech modalities.

nodes.name: Random ReLU on MNIST and SVHN
nodes.statement: Random ReLU feature models on $n=10^4$ subsets of MNIST and SVHN exhibit risk and norm curves qualitatively identical to RFF; tiny ridge $\lambda=4\cdot 10^{-6}$ added for SVHN stability.

nodes.name: Two-layer fully connected NN on MNIST
nodes.statement: Single-hidden-layer FC networks trained with weight-reuse SGD on $n=4\cdot 10^3$ MNIST exhibit double descent with interpolation threshold near $n \cdot K = 4 \cdot 10^4$ parameters; the same shape persists for CIFAR-10 (cat/dog) and for plain random initialization (with larger variance).

nodes.name: Random forest on MNIST (and SVHN, TIMIT)
nodes.section: 3 Decision trees and ensemble methods (Fig. 3); App. D
nodes.statement: Random forests on $n=10^4$ MNIST (and SVHN, TIMIT) regression tasks display double descent under the joint capacity index $(N_\mathsf{tree}, N_\mathsf{leaf}^\mathsf{max})$, both with and without bootstrap re-sampling.

nodes.name: $L_2$-boosted trees on MNIST and SVHN
nodes.statement: $L_2$-boosted random trees on $n=10^4$ MNIST and SVHN regression tasks display double descent; strong over-fitting under squared loss before the interpolation threshold, attenuated by high shrinkage.

nodes.name: Synthetic 1-D RFF (periodic Fourier basis)
nodes.statement: Periodic complex-valued functions on $[0,2\pi]$ with random Fourier basis $e_k(x)=\exp(\sqrt{-1}(k-1)x)$ chosen by sampling $p_k \propto 1/k^2$, target $h^* = \sum_k p_k e_k$, $n=256$, $\sigma^2$ noise: simulations confirm double descent with peak at $N=n$ at SNR $=\infty$ and SNR $=20$.

nodes.name: Random ReLU univariate fit ($N=40$ vs $N=4000$)
nodes.statement: Fitting 10 data points by Random ReLU features: with $N=40$, normalized coefficient norm $\approx 695$; with $N=4000$, norm $\approx 159$; the fit becomes visibly smoother as $N$ grows.

nodes.name: Equivalence of inductive biases for kernel machines
nodes.statement: For kernel machines, explicit norm minimization, SGD from zero initialization, and averaging Gaussian-process trajectories all lead to the same minimum-norm interpolant $\optninf$.

nodes.name: Optimization in the over-parametrized regime
nodes.statement: Local methods like SGD reliably converge to global minima of the training risk in over-parametrized models, so interpolating models are simultaneously low-test-risk and easy to optimize.

nodes.name: Historical absence of the double-descent curve
nodes.statement: The interpolation peak was historically masked by regularization, early stopping in NN training, and by use of RFF only in the computationally favorable regime $N \ll n$.

nodes.name: Margins theory limitation
nodes.statement: Margins theory partially explains why larger classes can help in classification but does not apply to regression and does not predict the second descent beyond the interpolation threshold.
